summary: Regime read: Potential pivot → tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 61% points tightening, 25% mixed, and 14% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (per Federal Reserve: The Fed - Inflation (PCE)). Fed communications are strongly tightening (per Federal Reserve: Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference - July 29, 2026). Employment is strongly easing and market pricing is strongly tightening.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction, one vote per event cluster (no magnitude averaging)
scoring.clustering: one vote per event_key; representative = max-weight source; keyless sources are singleton clusters

sources.title: How Can Employment Data Impact Fed Policy?
sources.evidence_text: August jobs report showed 142,000 additions and unemployment edged lower to 4.2%, supporting the view that the labor market is cooling.
sources.why_it_matters: Cooling labor data influenced the Fed's September decision to cut rates by 0.50%, illustrating the direct policy link.

sources.title: June PCE Report: PCE Inflation Index Up 2.6%, Stronger Than Expected
sources.evidence_text: Morningstar reported June PCE at 2.6% year over year and core PCE at 2.8% year over year, both above expectations.
sources.why_it_matters: An upside surprise in the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge makes faster policy easing less likely.

sources.title: US labor market stays afloat as unemployment rate falls to 4.2%
sources.evidence_text: The unemployment rate fell to 4.2% and the report said wage gains remained robust, even as job growth slowed and the market was not deteriorating sharply.
sources.why_it_matters: Firm labor data and solid wage growth reduce the urgency for Fed cuts and can keep policy restrictive for longer.

sources.title: Federal Reserve meeting calendars and information
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve's public calendar lists upcoming FOMC meeting dates and related information.
sources.why_it_matters: The meeting calendar anchors the exact policy decision date, which determines when market pricing for cuts or hikes becomes actionable.

sources.title: U.S. labor market adds 73,000 jobs in July while unemployment rate rises to 4.2%
sources.evidence_text: July payroll growth was below expectations, the unemployment rate rose to 4.2%, and prior months were revised down.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer labor-market print and downward revisions reduce pressure on the Fed to keep policy restrictive and support the case for cuts if inflation cooperates.

sources.title: Why a CPI surprise could trip up the Fed's rate-cutting plans
sources.evidence_text: The article says an upside CPI surprise could push the Fed toward a pause in rate cuts and keep the policy rate unchanged at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation surprises higher, the Fed is more likely to delay easing to preserve credibility on price stability.

sources.title: Inflation edges up, highlighting Fed's bumpy path to stable prices
sources.evidence_text: The article says October CPI rose to 2.6% year over year, which it described as a bump that still likely would not change the Fed's near-term course.
sources.why_it_matters: A firmer inflation print reduces the Fed's room to cut aggressively even if it does not fully reverse the easing cycle.

sources.title: Monetary Policy and the Fed's Framework Review
sources.evidence_text: Powell said policy was already much closer to neutral than a year earlier and that labor-market stability allowed the Fed to proceed carefully with further changes.
sources.why_it_matters: A closer-to-neutral stance and stable employment tend to keep the door open to additional easing if inflation cooperates.

sources.title: FOMC Press Conference, July 29, 2026
sources.evidence_text: This video records the July 29 FOMC press conference following the policy decision and statement release.
sources.why_it_matters: The recording is a primary source for the Fed's communication, but the transcript is the more useful item for reaction-function analysis.

sources.title: FedWatch - CME Group
sources.evidence_text: CME's FedWatch tool shows current market-implied probabilities for upcoming Fed meetings based on 30-day Fed funds futures.
sources.why_it_matters: If the tool shows fewer cuts or any hike probability, it implies the market expects a tighter Fed reaction function than earlier pricing.

sources.title: The Fed - Inflation (PCE)
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve states that it seeks to achieve 2 percent inflation over the longer run as measured by PCE.
sources.why_it_matters: Any sustained PCE reading above 2 percent reduces room for cuts because it implies inflation is still above the Fed’s stated goal.

sources.title: Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate
sources.evidence_text: The Dallas Fed’s trimmed mean PCE inflation rate was 2.4 percent over the 12 months ending in May, while headline PCE was 4.1 percent and core PCE was 3.4 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: A trimmed-mean measure above 2 percent suggests underlying inflation is still sticky, which argues for caution on rate cuts.

sources.title: Personal Consumption Expenditures: Chain-type Price Index
sources.evidence_text: FRED shows the PCE price index at 131.527 in May 2026, indicating the latest available monthly reading in the series is still elevated.
sources.why_it_matters: A still-rising PCE series reinforces that inflation is not yet back at target, limiting the Fed’s room to ease.

sources.title: Monetary Policy Report, July 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Fed reported that PCE inflation rose 4.1 percent over the 12 months ending in May, up from 2.5 percent a year earlier.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation running well above the Fed’s 2 percent objective argues against near-term easing and keeps policy biased toward restraint.

sources.title: Macro in a Minute: Inflation, Jobs, and the Fed
sources.evidence_text: The piece says stronger-than-expected inflation data led markets to align with the Fed's projected 75 basis points of cuts rather than pricing a more aggressive easing path.
sources.why_it_matters: When markets reprice toward fewer cuts, financial conditions tighten and the Fed sees less support for easing from market expectations.

sources.title: Fed rate cut unlikely; would be 'like throwing oil on the fire ...'
sources.evidence_text: The article says top economists expect rate cuts to be off the table for 2026, framing the Fed as unlikely to ease further in the near term.
sources.why_it_matters: If expectations shift toward no cuts, that indicates inflation concerns are dominating the reaction function over growth support.

sources.title: 30 Day Federal Funds Overview
sources.evidence_text: CME describes the 30-Day Federal Funds futures contract as the underlying market input used to gauge expectations for the federal funds rate.
sources.why_it_matters: This contract is the pricing basis for FedWatch, so moves in it reflect shifting expectations for cuts versus a more restrictive policy path.

sources.title: Fed Rate Monitor
sources.evidence_text: The monitor shows a majority probability of a hold at the July FOMC meeting and also assigns meaningful probability to a quarter-point hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A meaningful hike probability indicates the market has shifted toward a tighter policy path than a cuts-only baseline.

sources.title: Fed Decision in July? Trading Odds & Predictions 2026
sources.evidence_text: The event page says market-implied odds favor no change at 79.5%, with 19.4% pricing for a 25 bp hike and negligible cut odds.
sources.why_it_matters: If market participants mostly price a hold but still assign meaningful hike odds, the reaction function is being pulled toward tighter policy rather than easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve: Extended pause guidance – UOB
sources.evidence_text: UOB said the Fed is widely expected to keep rates unchanged at the July meeting, while OIS pricing assigned roughly a one-third probability to a 25bp hike.
sources.why_it_matters: If the market assigns meaningful hike odds into the next FOMC, that implies less room for near-term easing and a slightly tighter reaction-function signal.

sources.title: What's The Fed's Next Move?
sources.evidence_text: J.P. Morgan says the Fed should remain on hold for the rest of 2026 and sees the first hike only in September 2027, despite noting that markets are pricing a 2026 hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold-for-longer forecast means the baseline policy path is not easing soon, even if it does not call for an immediate hike.

sources.title: US 2 Year Treasury Bond Note Yield - Quote - Chart
sources.evidence_text: Trading Economics projected the US 2-year Treasury yield to end the quarter near 4.12% and to be around 3.92% in 12 months.
sources.why_it_matters: A modestly lower 12-month front-end forecast suggests only limited easing is priced, but the signal is model-based rather than an official market measure.

sources.title: The Fed’s Favorite Measure Of Inflation Cooled Down In June
sources.evidence_text: The June PCE report showed headline inflation at 3.7% year over year and core PCE at 3.3%, both below the prior month.
sources.why_it_matters: Cooling inflation eases pressure on the Fed and modestly improves the case for eventual cuts, though levels remain above target.

sources.title: Survey of Consumer Expectations
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.evidence_text: The New York Fed’s consumer expectations survey tracks medium-term inflation expectations that are relevant for assessing whether inflation beliefs remain anchored.
sources.why_it_matters: If expectations stay anchored, the Fed has more room to ease; if they drift up, that would tighten the policy outlook.

sources.title: CPI Home
sources.evidence_text: The BLS CPI program is the official source for monthly consumer inflation data, including shelter and services components.
sources.why_it_matters: Fresh CPI readings on shelter and services help determine whether inflation is decelerating enough for the Fed to cut further.

sources.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept the policy rate unchanged at 3.50% to 3.75%, said inflation remains elevated relative to its 2% goal, and noted three dissents in favor of a 25 bp hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold with a hawkish dissent and elevated inflation language signals fewer near-term cuts and a higher bar for easing.

sources.title: Statement on My FOMC Dissent
sources.evidence_text: A Minneapolis Fed policymaker said she dissented because she preferred to raise the federal funds target range by 0.25 percentage point this week.
sources.why_it_matters: An explicit rate-hike dissent indicates concern that inflation or other conditions warrant tighter policy than the majority chose.

sources.title: Fed meeting recap: July 2026
sources.evidence_text: CNBC reported that markets expected the Fed to keep rates steady at the July meeting and focused on Powell's guidance for future cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: Market expectations around a hold with uncertain follow-up matter because they influence financial conditions and the perceived urgency of easing.

sources.title: Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference - July 29, 2026
sources.evidence_text: Warsh said the Committee kept rates unchanged, described the economy as resilient, and emphasized that inflation remains elevated relative to the 2 percent goal.
sources.why_it_matters: That framing suggests the Fed is prioritizing inflation containment over near-term easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: The Fed states that monetary policy is directed toward maximum employment, stable prices, and moderate long-term interest rates.
sources.why_it_matters: This is the framework that governs how incoming inflation and employment data are weighed in rate decisions.

sources.title: H.15 - Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - July 30, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve’s H.15 release shows the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.17% on July 30, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher 2-year yield generally means the market is pricing a higher expected policy path, which supports fewer cuts or possible hikes.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims increase less than expected
sources.evidence_text: Initial jobless claims rose by 9,000 to 197,000 for the week ended July 25, and continuing claims fell to 1.782 million for the prior week.
sources.why_it_matters: The report shows claims remained low enough to suggest labor market stability, which does not strongly pressure the Fed toward immediate cuts or hikes.

sources.title: Fed's Preferred Inflation Gauge Cools to 3.7%
sources.evidence_text: The June PCE inflation rate fell to 3.7 percent year over year, while core PCE eased to 3.3 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: A cooling PCE print supports some disinflation progress, but inflation remains far above target so it does not clearly force cuts.

sources.title: June 2026 PCE inflation falls 0.1%, consumer spending up 0.3%
sources.evidence_text: The BEA reported that headline PCE declined 0.1% in June while core PCE rose 0.1% on the month and 3.3% year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: The month-over-month cooling supports the case for patience, although core inflation still running above target limits how far the Fed can ease.

sources.title: Fed Policymaker Comments Raise the Stakes for Inflation Data
sources.evidence_text: PIMCO said the June inflation cooling removed a rate hike from the next meeting's consideration, but it still expects the Fed to stay on hold through 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: This framing implies inflation has eased enough to reduce near-term hike odds, yet not enough to justify cuts under the Fed's price-stability mandate.

sources.title: CPI Inflation Contributions from Goods and Services
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
sources.evidence_text: The San Francisco Fed’s inflation decomposition tool shows how goods and services contributions can be monitored to assess whether inflation pressure is broad-based or fading.
sources.why_it_matters: Broad services contribution would support a slower pace of easing because it signals persistent underlying inflation.

sources.title: Prices, Wages and Workers: The Recent U.S. Inflation Experience
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.evidence_text: The St. Louis Fed reiterates that the FOMC’s price-stability goal is 2% inflation as measured by the annual change in the PCE price index.
sources.why_it_matters: Any inflation or wage signal above that benchmark reduces the Fed’s tolerance for additional easing.

sources.title: 30 Day Federal Funds Futures Quotes
sources.evidence_text: CME's 30-day Fed Funds futures quotes are the input market for estimating whether traders are pricing cuts, holds, or hikes.
sources.why_it_matters: Fed funds futures directly encode the expected policy path, so a move from cuts to hikes is a tightening signal for the Fed reaction function.

sources.title: Treasury yields jump as traders reduce expectations for any 2026 Fed rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: Traders reduced expectations for 2026 rate cuts, while the 2-year Treasury yield rose to its highest level since July of the prior year and futures began to price possible hikes.
sources.why_it_matters: Higher policy-sensitive yields and fewer priced cuts suggest markets see the Fed needing to stay restrictive or potentially tighten further.

sources.title: United States - Monthly Data
sources.evidence_text: The BLS state-level dashboard shows the unemployment rate at 4.3% and payroll gains slowing to 172,000 in May 2026, with average hourly earnings rising 3.7% year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: Slower payroll growth with contained wage gains usually leans toward easier policy if inflation is not reaccelerating.

sources.title: August | 2026 - FRED Blog
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.evidence_text: The FRED Blog notes that its August discussion uses monthly employment data reported by the BLS.
sources.why_it_matters: FRED commentary can help contextualize the labor trend, but the Fed reacts primarily to the underlying official data.

sources.title: Advisors take note: PCE cools in June, but don't expect the Fed to turn dovish yet
sources.evidence_text: The article says June PCE cooled but still should not be read as a signal that the Fed is ready to turn dovish.
sources.why_it_matters: This framing suggests the data is improving but not enough to shift the Fed’s reaction function decisively toward easing.

sources.title: 5-Year, 5-Year Forward Inflation Expectation Rate (T5YIFR)
sources.evidence_text: The 5-year, 5-year forward inflation expectation rate was 2.18% on 2026-06-23.
sources.why_it_matters: Well-anchored market inflation compensation supports the case for easing if realized inflation continues to cool.

sources.title: Lower-Than-Expected Inflation Keeps Fed On Track For October Rate Cut
sources.evidence_text: The article says September CPI rose 3.0% year over year, below the expected 3.1%, and argues that this left the Fed on track for cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A downside inflation surprise reduces the immediate need for restraint and supports further easing if labor-market conditions also soften.

sources.title: Tame US inflation gives the Fed room for more rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: ING argued that softer November CPI gives the Fed room for earlier and faster cuts in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A lower inflation trajectory widens the Fed's ability to prioritize labor-market support without breaching its price-stability goal.

sources.title: The Fed - Live Video
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve was broadcasting a live video feed on its site.
sources.why_it_matters: A live Fed event can move expectations if it includes remarks on inflation, employment, or the policy path.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - News & Events
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's News & Events page was available as the main hub for current announcements and speeches.
sources.why_it_matters: This is the official index for any new speeches, statements, or events that could affect the reaction function.

sources.title: The Fed - July 28-29, 2026 FOMC Meeting
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range unchanged at its July 28-29 meeting and reaffirmed its commitment to price stability.
sources.why_it_matters: Holding rates steady while emphasizing price stability signals the Committee is not yet ready to ease further despite remaining inflation concerns.

sources.title: FedWatch Tool User Guide
sources.evidence_text: CME says the FedWatch Tool analyzes 30-Day Fed Fund futures prices to show the probability of different FOMC rate outcomes.
sources.why_it_matters: Because the tool is based on futures pricing, it is useful for identifying whether market pricing is drifting toward fewer cuts or hikes.
